concepts.description_formal: A differential equation relates a function of an independent variable to that function's derivatives; a first order equation involves the function and its first derivative only.
concepts.description_plain: A differential equation says how fast a quantity changes in terms of the quantity itself, the independent variable, or both.
concepts.name: Differential equation as a relation between a function and its derivatives

concepts.description_formal: A function is a solution to a differential equation on an interval when substituting the function and its derivative into the equation yields a true statement for every input in that interval.
concepts.description_plain: A candidate function is a solution exactly when differentiating it and substituting reproduces the equation.
concepts.name: Verification of a proposed solution

concepts.description_formal: The general solution of a first order differential equation is a family indexed by a constant; a differential equation may have infinitely many solutions (BC-EK-FUN-7B2).
concepts.description_plain: One differential equation is satisfied by infinitely many functions, one through each point of the plane it covers.
concepts.name: Families of solutions
concepts.notation: general solution; family of solutions; the constant C

concepts.description_formal: A slope field is a graphical representation of a first order differential equation on a finite set of points in the plane, each segment carrying the slope the equation gives at that point.
concepts.description_plain: A slope field draws a short segment at each of finitely many points, with the slope the equation assigns to that point.
concepts.name: Slope field as a plot of derivative values
concepts.notation: slope field; lattice point; segment slope

concepts.description_formal: Solutions to a differential equation are functions or families of functions whose graphs are everywhere tangent to the segments of the slope field.
concepts.description_plain: A solution is a curve that follows the segments, and the field shows how solutions behave without any solving.
concepts.name: Solution curves read off a slope field

concepts.description_formal: Euler's method approximates a solution by advancing from a point with the increment equal to the step size multiplied by the derivative evaluated at the current approximation, repeating from the new point.
concepts.description_plain: Euler's method steps along tangent lines, using each new approximation as the starting point for the next step.
concepts.name: Euler's method as repeated local linearisation
concepts.notation: step size; y sub n plus one

concepts.description_formal: A differential equation whose right side factors as a function of the independent variable multiplied by a function of the dependent variable can be rearranged so each side involves one variable, then antidifferentiated.
concepts.description_plain: When the equation factors into a part in one variable and a part in the other, both sides can be antidifferentiated separately.
concepts.name: Separation of variables
concepts.notation: separated form; one constant of integration

concepts.description_formal: A general solution describes infinitely many solutions; exactly one particular solution passes through a given point, and substituting that point determines the constant of integration.
concepts.description_plain: The initial condition picks one curve out of the family and settles the constant and the sign.
concepts.name: Particular solution selected by an initial condition

concepts.description_formal: Solutions to differential equations may be subject to domain restrictions, taken as the largest interval containing the initial input on which the solution expression is defined and continuous.
concepts.description_plain: A particular solution is valid only on the interval around the initial point where the expression stays defined.
concepts.name: Domain restrictions on a particular solution
concepts.notation: domain restriction; interval containing the initial input

concepts.description_formal: The statement that the rate of change of a quantity is proportional to the size of the quantity is the differential equation dy/dt equal to k y, whose solution with y equal to y sub 0 at t equal to zero is y equal to y sub 0 times e to the k t.
concepts.description_plain: When the rate of change is proportional to the amount present, the amount is an exponential function of the independent variable.
concepts.name: Exponential growth and decay model
concepts.notation: dy/dt = ky; y = y sub 0 e^(kt)

concepts.description_formal: The statement that the rate of change of a quantity is jointly proportional to the size of the quantity and the difference between the quantity and the carrying capacity is the differential equation dy/dt equal to k y times the quantity a minus y.
concepts.description_plain: When growth is limited, the rate depends on both the amount present and how much room is left.
concepts.name: Logistic differential equation

concepts.description_formal: The limiting value of a logistic model as the independent variable grows without bound is the carrying capacity, and the dependent variable changes fastest at half the carrying capacity; both follow from the equation and the initial condition without solving it.
concepts.description_plain: A logistic model has a ceiling, and the quantity grows fastest when it is halfway there.
concepts.name: Carrying capacity and the point of fastest change
concepts.notation: carrying capacity; half of the carrying capacity

prerequisites.description_plain: Exponentiating both sides of a logarithmic equation, taking a logarithm of both sides of an exponential equation, and isolating the variable afterwards.
prerequisites.failure_signature: Student reaches a correct antiderivative equation and cannot reach an explicit expression for the dependent variable.
prerequisites.name: Solving an equation that contains a logarithm or an exponential

prerequisites.description_plain: Reading dy/dx as an object that can be split into dy and dx for the purpose of separating a differential equation, and writing the differential on every integral.

prerequisites.notes: Non-calculus prerequisite inferred from the demands of the essential knowledge statements of this unit.

prerequisites.description_plain: Translating the phrase proportional to into a constant multiple, and jointly proportional to into a constant times a product of two quantities.
